Disrumpo.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **A preset loaded from the browser kept the previous preset's shape settings** — Loading from the preset browser did not run the same code as a project reload. Each node remembers its shape settings for every distortion type, and the sound engine kept the previous preset's settings for every type except the one in use, so changing a node's type afterwards (by hand or by automation) played stale settings, and the next project save stored them. A browser load now takes the same path as a project reload, and the browser's Save stores exactly what the sound engine holds.
- **The Chaos distortion repeated a short cycle instead of evolving** *(shared DSP)* — In the Lorenz model at 44.1 and 48 kHz, the attractor was stepped too coarsely, briefly overshot its safety bound and was restarted about 36 times a second, so the distortion repeated the same 28 ms pattern. The attractor is now stepped finely enough at every sample rate and speed, and only a truly runaway state is restarted.
- **The Stepped modulation curve overshot its amount by a third** *(shared DSP)* — With the source at full scale (a macro at 100 %, a square LFO), a route or macro with the Stepped curve gave 4/3 of its amount. Its top step is now exactly the amount, so such routes move less than before at full scale.
- **Changing a modulation route's source or destination could jump** *(shared DSP)* — When a route switched source, destination or curve, it briefly applied the old route's amount to the new destination, which could cause a short burst or jump. A changed route now starts from its own amount.
- **Small load fixes** — A new instance ran the Rungler at 200 Hz, outside its range, until its Rate knob was moved; it now starts at the 4.09 Hz the knob shows. A project could restore Folds and Bit Depth between the steps their knobs offer; they now load on a step, as a browser load does.

Gradus.notes_markdown:
### Changed

- **Swing now plays long step first, and keeps swinging with the host playing** *(shared arp engine)* — Free-running, each swung pair played its short step first while the gates and ratchets were sized for the long one. With the host transport running, Gradus re-locked to the host every block, which undid the swing and could fire two notes a few milliseconds apart. Each step now lasts its own swung length, the long step comes first in both cases, and gates and ratchets fit the step they belong to. Every swung preset and project swings the other way round from before.

### Fixed

- **A gate above 100 % on a single held key played staccato** *(shared arp engine)* — When the same pitch was struck again while its previous note was still held, that older note's note-off cut the new note at the old gate length, so a legato gate (101-200 %) turned into 50 % notes. A re-struck pitch now ends the old note first and the new note keeps its full gate.
- **The first note after a pause could come late** *(shared arp engine)* — After all keys were released, the step counter stopped where it was, so the first note of the next phrase waited out the rest of that old step: up to 2 seconds at slow free rates. The first step now fires in the block the key is pressed.
- **The arp drifted off tempo when not following the host** *(shared arp engine)* — Step lengths derived from the tempo were cut down to a whole sample instead of rounded, so with the transport stopped or a free-running arp each step could be one sample short and the pattern drifted against the tempo. Step lengths now round to the nearest sample and swung pairs add up exactly.
- **Editing a Modifier lane step saved the wrong value** *(shared UI)* — A step clicked, pasted or transformed in the Modifier lane was saved as 17 times its flag value (the lane and the parameter used different scales). The sound was the same, but the saved value differed from the factory presets. The lane now saves the flags themselves.
- **Speed-curve depth was 0 after reopening a project** — After a project reload the arpeggiator played every lane's speed curve at depth 0 until a speed-curve control was touched. The saved depths now apply as soon as the project loads.
- **The Ratchet and Condition lanes swapped their speed-curve depths** — Each lane's depth knob drove the other lane. Each now drives its own. In older projects a curve drawn on the Ratchet tab may now show on the Condition tab, the lane it always played on.
- **A preset loaded from the browser and one restored by the host could play differently** — Loading from the preset browser did not run the same code as a host restore, so ratchet shuffle, lane speeds and a few clamped values could differ between the two. Both now load identically. The factory presets now store the ratchet shuffle they play (50, 66.67 or 75 %).
- **Resetting a lane speed to its default set it to 0.25x** — The eight lane-speed controls reported 0.25x to the host as their default, so a host "reset to default" (or double-click reset) slowed the lane to a quarter. Their default is now 1x, the speed a new instance starts at.

Innexus.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **A preset loaded from the preset browser now loads all of it** — The preset browser read presets with a second, incomplete reader that never reached the sound engine directly: the envelope (ADSR) settings, voice mode, modulator tempo sync, the physical-model, impact, waveguide, bow, body and sympathetic settings, the stored memory slots and their envelopes were left as they were. A browser load now takes the same path as a project reload, so the whole preset is restored, including its stored sample, which is loaded again from its saved location.
- **The modulator Sync switches and note values showed the wrong setting after a project reload** — Reopening a project restored Mod 1 and Mod 2 Sync and Note Value in the sound, but the controls showed their defaults. They now show the restored values.

Iterum.notes_markdown:
### Added

- **Four new Spectral spread curves** — Spread Curve now also offers Exponential (the lows and mids return together, then the highs trail out), Steps (eight bands, each a separate echo, like a multitap arpeggiating the spectrum), Scatter (third-octave bands in a fixed shuffled order, the same on every echo) and Random (the bands keep gliding to new delays, so no two echoes are alike).
- **Two new Spectral spread directions** — Spread Direction now also offers Edges In (the lows and highs return first and the echo closes in on the mids) and Cross (the echo sweeps up on the left and down on the right at the same time).

### Changed

- **Spectral mode's Spread now sweeps through the sound** *(shared DSP)* — Spread was laid out evenly in Hz, so everything below about 2 kHz, most of a mix, shared the first tenth of the spread time: Low->High came back as one plain echo with a faint treble trail, and High->Low and Center Out as one plain later echo. Spread is now laid out by octave, from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, so each echo audibly sweeps from low to high, high to low, or out from the middle. Logarithmic now really differs from Linear: it gives the low octaves most of the spread. Every patch that uses Spread sounds different.
- **Spread Direction and Spread Curve are menus** — With five and six entries they no longer fit as segment buttons, so both are drop-down menus in the Spread section. Saved patches keep their direction and curve.

### Fixed

- **Spectral mode's echo got 1 to 6 dB quieter with Spread** *(shared DSP)* — Each sound covers several neighbouring frequency bands; with Spread they left the delay at different moments, their phases stopped lining up and the sound partly cancelled itself, by an amount that jumped around with the exact Spread setting. The bands of one sound now leave together, and the echo keeps its level with Spread on.

Membrum.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **A kit loaded from the browser did not fully replace the previous kit** — Loading a kit from the kit browser ran a separate copy of the kit loader in the editor instead of the one a project reload uses. It skipped the voice and coupling flush, so drums still ringing from the previous kit could carry over as a tonal beep or a ring that did not stop. It also left each pad's noise-layer level and the "default" body damping as they were, and did not update the macros. A browser load now runs the same code as a project reload.
- **A pad preset changed the pad's on/off state and pan, and skipped its noise layer** — Loading a pad preset onto a pad overwrote the pad's enabled state and pan, which a pad preset is meant to leave alone, and did not apply the preset's noise-layer level. Pad presets now load through the sound engine's own pad-preset code: enabled and pan are kept and the noise layer is applied.

Profundum.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **Sample & Hold and Smooth Random morph cycles repeated too soon** — The random generator behind these two cycle shapes overflowed and cycled after about 79,000 values instead of running its full sequence. It now runs the full sequence, so these shapes play a different random pattern than before.
- **The stereo field's band split lost precision at low frequencies** — Its crossover filters now run in double precision, which removes a small level error at low split frequencies, largest at high sample rates.
- **A possible crash when a host shut Profundum down with its window still open** — If a host shut down the plugin's controller before closing the editor window, the update banner kept checking for updates, twice a second, through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The update check now stays alive until the window is gone.
- **A possible crash when opening the preset browser after a host shut Profundum down with its window still open** — In the same situation, clicking Presets read the preset list through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The preset list now stays alive until the window is gone.

- **Long preset descriptions were cut off in the preset browser** — The description under the preset list was a single line, so a long one ended mid-word at the edge. It now wraps onto up to three lines, ending with "…" if it is longer still, and hovering over it shows the whole text.

### Changed

- **Built with VST3 SDK 3.8.1.**

Seraphis.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **The FX delay's Feedback did almost nothing after the first repeat** *(shared DSP)* — The spectral delay's feedback limiter worked on unscaled FFT values, so it squashed every recirculated frequency down to the same tiny level: the repeats after the first fell away by tens of dB and lost their tone colour. The limiter now works in the signal's own scale, so Feedback sustains the repeats as set and keeps their spectrum. Presets and projects with FX delay feedback above 0 repeat noticeably longer than before.
- **The FX delay stepped at every analysis frame** *(shared DSP)* — The spectral delay overlapped its frames without a synthesis window, so with feedback its output jumped at every frame edge. It now uses matched analysis and synthesis windows, and the steps are gone.
- **The FX delay's return fade moved in steps** — The 20 ms fade of the FX delay's return level was updated once per processing slice, so it moved as a staircase with a small jump at each slice. It now moves sample by sample.

Vorago.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **Notes held by the latch or the sustain pedal kept sounding after a browser preset load** — Loading a preset from the preset browser only changed the controls; the sound engine's own load code never ran, so latched and sustained notes from the previous preset carried on into the new one. A browser load now runs the same code as a project reload: it releases those notes and resets sustain and channel pressure. Older presets and projects are also converted by one shared routine on both paths, so they load the same way from the browser and from the host.
